newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's MTRC proposes two new MTR lines.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's MTRC proposes two new MTR lines.

text.p: Hong Kong's Mass Transit Railway Corp (MTRC) said on Monday it had proposed two new lines to the government as part of its plans to extend the territory's railways.

The East Kowloon line would run from Diamond Hill in Kowloon to a new station at the Exhibition and Convention Centre in Wan Chai on Hong Kong Island via Kai Tak, To Kwa Wan, Ma Tau Wei, Ho Man Tin and Hung Hom.
The North Island line, running across the North side of Hong Kong Island, would link North Point in the East to Tamer in the West and join up with the airport railway line.
An MTRC spokeswoman said construction costs at current prices are estimated at HK$30-35 billion.
"It is just at a very preliminary stage," the spokeswoman said, adding that the MTRC hopes to have the two new lines completed by 2006.
"It takes about four years for construction. Before that we have to sort out all the details with the government," she said.
